“To them, you’re just an ATM.

I’ve been visiting this clinic since 2007. Back then, it was a small setup with just one shop, and the treatment was genuinely good — probably because it was the beginning of their business. But now, the clinic has grown massively, with several doctors working under the main vet. And sadly, so has their greed.

Even a basic routine check-up now costs ₹3,000 to ₹4,000. It’s all about money. They prescribe unnecessary medicines just to inflate the bill.

I recently lost my beloved pet. I wouldn’t mind paying more if it meant quality care — but despite being charged ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 daily, my pet’s condition only worsened. She couldn’t even drink water. The doctor himself admitted she wouldn’t survive, yet they still prescribed 15 days of medication — knowing she might not even make it through the night.

My advice: if your pet is seriously ill, don’t go there. They will exploit your fear and your love to make money.

I truly believe that if my pet had received the right treatment at the right time, she might still be with me. But the doctors were too busy chasing profits — and I lost the love of my life.”

featured_reviews.name: Beena Mathur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I'm truly sorry for your loss. Losing a beloved pet like Moiza is heartbreaking, and it's especially painful when it feels preventable. Below is a draft of your review—clear, respectful, and informative to help other pet parents make more informed decisions:

---

**Review for Prolife Vets, Malad West (Dr. Akshata)**
⭐☆☆☆☆

I’m writing this with a heavy heart. I recently lost my beloved cat, Moiza, due to what I believe was a case of medical negligence and misdiagnosis at Prolife Vets, Malad West, under the care of Dr. Akshata.

Moiza had stopped eating for two days, and we immediately took her to Prolife. Dr. Akshata examined her and diagnosed her with dental issues, saying her teeth were "spoiled" and that’s why she couldn’t eat. A blood test was conducted, and I was told that the reports were *normal*. She prescribed only basic medications to stimulate appetite, with no further action or urgency.

We tried to force-feed Moiza over the next few days, but she was clearly getting worse. On the third day, we rushed her back, and Dr. Akshata changed her statement, saying, "Daat itne bhi burey nahi hai ke kuch kha hi na sake," dismissing the initial diagnosis. Still, no serious treatment or investigation was done.

Concerned, we immediately took Moiza to another vet. To our shock, we found that the blood reports—previously described as normal—actually showed extremely high WBC counts, indicating a serious underlying infection or illness. The new vet started emergency treatment, but by then, it was too late. Moiza passed away.

What’s more painful is knowing that earlier intervention *could* have saved her. The negligence in reading and explaining the blood report, the casual attitude ("WBC thoda high hai but chalega"), and the lack of urgency or empathy from Dr. Akshata cost Moiza her life.

Additionally, the environment at Prolife during our visits was completely unprofessional. The Akshata  and staff were laughing and cracking jokes while I was there  giving saline to my pet on my 1st visit as doctor akshata told to give saline 1st visit as she was not eating anything ,with a visibly sick pet and in emotional distress. The receptionist was also dismissive.

I had faith in Prolife only because of Dr. Gadge, who has always been professional and compassionate. Unfortunately, he was not available during Moiza’s visits, as informed by the receptionist and I had no option but to consult with Dr. Akshata.

This review is not out of anger, but out of deep pain and a genuine desire to warn fellow pet parents: **Please be extremely cautious when consulting for serious health issues. Seek a second opinion, and don’t ignore your instincts if something feels wrong.**

Moiza deserved better. She would likely still be with us if proper diagnosis and urgency were shown from day one.

Necessary consultations, prescriptions, medications, blood tests, IV fluids, and supportive treatments were advised according to the kitten’s condition at that time. We completely understand the grief and distress associated with losing a young pet. However, we strongly deny allegations of negligence or intentional carelessness by our doctors or staff. featured_reviews.review_text:
​​I am extremely disappointed with the care provided to my cat, Pintu, at this clinic. We brought her in with the very specific and concerning symptoms that she was completely refusing to eat and constantly hiding. Despite spending 11k on diagnostics and treatment, she is still facing the exact same issues with zero improvement—she is still not eating, still hiding, and still suffering.

​To make matters worse, yesterday, at the exact moment we were leaving the clinic to take her back home, they suddenly demanded an additional 7k. They claimed she has an infection and that we would have to pay this extra amount for the "next procedure." Springing massive, unexpected financial demands at the last minute—before the initial 11k treatment has even shown a single positive result for her main symptoms—feels completely unprofessional and exploitative.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mr. Salvi, we are surprised to see this review as you haven't visited our premises yourself and it was Ms. Padawe who brought Pintu in. We are unaware of how you are connected to this case but we would still like to clarify.

We are sorry that you feel this way and would like to bring you some relief by actually narrating what really happened at our premises. Pintu was presented with inappetence and weakness, and all diagnostics, treatment plans, and estimated costs were discussed, signed and approved before proceeding by Ms. Padawe. Throughout her diagnostic tests and treatment, we provided updates regarding her condition as she was boarded with us for medical supervision through the day.

The statement that an additional ₹7,000 was suddenly demanded before leaving is completely inaccurate. The amount was discussed and approved beforehand and was for a specific diagnostic test that was strongly suggested because we needed to arrive at a definitive diagnosis with no prior history of an indoor-outdoor cat like Pintu. 

It is also important to understand that cats suffering from infectious or systemic illnesses may not recover completely within a single day of treatment. Improvement often requires several days of consistent medication, supportive care, and follow-up monitoring.

Regarding the concern that Pintu ran away after receiving her medication, there is no medical basis to conclude that the prescribed medication caused her to leave the house, as you mentioned that she is an indoor outdoor cat already. Cats experiencing illness, stress, or discomfort may hide or become less visible, and this behavior was part of the original concerns for which she was presented, infact you mentioned  she was so weak that she couldn't move and after treatment she had enough energy to run away from home when tried to feed medication. At the time, we provided guidance and continued to assist you through messages regarding her care at home multiple times.

We also provided advice regarding medication administration and feeding, and recommended that Pintu be brought back for treatment if you don't see an improvement in her condition after she returned home. Unfortunately, the recommended follow-up treatment was not carried out by you.

We fully understand how distressing it is when a pet is unwell. However, it is important that the outcome of a medical case be assessed based on the complete course of treatment and follow-up rather than just the first 12 hours after discharge.

Our team remains committed to providing transparent communication, appropriate medical care, and support to every patient and pet owner.  

After leaving us the above review Ms. Padawe still reached out to ask for more assistance and we still happily obliged as it's Pintu's wellbeing that has always been our priority. 
We sincerely wish Pintu a full and speedy recovery and honestly hope that you follow through with the recommended diagnostics and treatment wherever you choose to take Pintu
